raw_text:
Thanks — below is a 12-week progressive, full-gym strength programme tailored for a 42-year-old male desk worker, post L4–L5 disc herniation (8 months ago), currently asymptomatic. It follows the constraint: avoid heavy spinal loading and avoid loaded spinal flexion (e.g., heavy barbell back squats with deep flexion, heavy bent-over loaded flexion movements). The plan emphasizes spine-safe loading patterns, core control, posterior chain development, mobility, and progressive overload using safer alternatives (e.g., goblet/suitcase/zercher where appropriate, split/leg-focused unilateral work, machines, RDL variants from hips with neutral spine, and anti-flexion/anti-rotation core work). It also includes conditioning, mobility, recovery, and high-level nutrition guidance.

Structure overview
- 3 phases, each 4 weeks (12 weeks total).
- Frequency: 4 gym sessions/week (2 upper, 2 lower; one lower focuses more on single‑leg and hip hinge; one upper emphasizes horizontal/vertical pushes and pulls). Optional 1 low-impact cardio/mobility session.
- Progression: Start conservative (focus on technique, low-moderate load), then build intensity/volume, and finish with higher intensity while still respecting spine constraints.
- Load guidance: work in RPE 6–8 for most sets. Use weight that allows control and neutral spine. No heavy barbell back squats, heavy bent-over rows loaded with spinal flexion, or heavy loaded spinal flexion movements. Use machines, goblet/box squat, Bulgarian split squats, L-sit/progressive core holds, trap-bar deadlift with strict hinge or Romanian deadlift from rack with light-moderate loads focusing on hip hinge.
- Rest: 60–120s between strength sets depending on intensity/goal. 30–60s between accessory sets.

Initial screening reminders (trainer checklist before starting)
- Confirm physio clearance for resisted hip hinge variations (RDL/trap-bar) and unilateral leg work.
- Confirm absence of neurologic symptoms (pain, numbness, sciatica). Stop and refer back to physio if symptoms recur.
- Emphasize diaphragmatic breathing, bracing (neutral spine), and controlled tempo on eccentric phases.
- Warm-up each session (10–12 minutes): light cardio 5 min, dynamic mobility for hips/thoracic spine/shoulders, 2–3 movement prep sets of the main lift at light load.

Phase 1 — Foundation & movement quality (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: rebuild tolerance to load, engrain neutral spine and hip-hinge, strengthen core and glutes, improve thoracic mobility, build baseline conditioning.

Weekly schedule (4 gym days + optional active recovery)
- Day A — Upper 1 (Horizontal emphasis)
- Day B — Lower 1 (Hip hinge & unilateral)
- Day C — Upper 2 (Vertical emphasis)
- Day D — Lower 2 (Squat pattern via goblet/box & posterior chain)
- Optional Day E — 20–30 min bike/row + mobility

Weeks 1–4: session details

Day A — Upper 1 (Horizontal push/pull)
1. Warm-up + wall slides / band pull-aparts / T-spine rotations
2. Incline dumbbell press — 3 sets x 8–10 reps (RPE 6–7)
3. Seated cable row (chest supported if available) — 3 x 8–10
4. Flat dumbbell press (light) or machine chest press — 2 x 10–12
5. Chest-supported single-arm dumbbell row — 3 x 8–10 each
6. Face pulls — 3 x 12–15
7. Pallof press (anti-rotation, cable) — 3 x 10–12 each side
8. Farmer carry (light–moderate) 3 x 30–45 s (neutral spine, braced)

Day B — Lower 1 (Hip hinge & unilateral)
1. Warm-up + hip CARs, glute bridges
2. Trap-bar deadlift (light; emphasis on hip hinge, not maximal) — 3 x 6–8 (RPE 6)
   - If trap-bar not available, perform RDL from a rack or Romanian deadlift with dumbbells, focus on neutral spine.
3. Bulgarian split squat — 3 x 8–10 each leg (use DBs)
4. Single-leg Romanian deadlift (dumbbell) — 2 x 8–10 each
5. Glute bridge or hip thrust (bodyweight -> light load) — 3 x 10–12
6. Deadbug progressing to slow bird-dog — 3 x 8–10 each
7. Calf raise (standing or seated) — 3 x 12–15

Day C — Upper 2 (Vertical emphasis)
1. Warm-up + banded shoulder warm-up
2. Seated/standing dumbbell shoulder press — 3 x 8–10
3. Lat pulldown (neutral/underhand optional) — 3 x 8–10
4. One-arm cable row or single-arm machine row — 3 x 10 each
5. Lateral raises (light) — 3 x 12–15
6. Incline Y/T/I on bench or prone Y’s — 3 x 10 total
7. Farmer carry or suitcase carry — 3 x 30–45 s

Day D — Lower 2 (Goblet/box squat & posterior chain)
1. Warm-up + ankle/hip mobility
2. Goblet squat to box (controlled depth) — 3 x 8–10 (use DB or kettlebell)
3. Step-ups (box or bench) — 3 x 8–10 each leg
4. Good morning (light, no spinal flexion; hip hinge with neutral spine; can be a band or machine variant) — 3 x 10
5. Seated leg curl (machine) or single-leg curl — 3 x 10–12
6. Side plank progressions — 3 x 20–40 s each side
7. Farmer carry variations (suitcase carry for anti-rotation) — 3 x 30–45 s

Progression notes for Phase 1
- Use moderate loads allowing controlled technique. Increase load when able to complete prescribed reps for two consecutive sessions with good form.
- Emphasize thoracic mobility drills and deep breathing/bracing.

Phase 2 — Strength & capacity (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: increase load and intensity while maintaining spine safety; introduce heavier but safer loading (trap-bar, front-loaded or goblet variations), more challenging unilateral and posterior chain work, higher core loads (anti-extension/anti-rotation).

Weekly schedule remains 4 days. Slightly higher intensity and volume.

Example Week structure: Day A Upper, Day B Lower, Day C Upper, Day D Lower

Weeks 5–8: session details (changes/highlights)

Day A — Upper 1
1. Warm-up
2. Flat dumbbell press or cable press — 4 x 6–8 (increase load)
3. Chest-supported row or seated machine row — 4 x 6–8
4. Incline single-arm DB press — 3 x 8 each
5. High-rep face pulls — 3 x 12–15
6. Pallof press (heavier band or cable) — 3 x 10 each
7. Carry progression: heavy farmer carry 3 x 45–60 s

Day B — Lower 1
1. Warm-up
2. Trap-bar deadlift (moderate-heavy; keep hinge and neutral spine) — 4 x 5 (RPE 7–8)
3. Reverse lunge (walking or standing) — 3 x 8–10 each
4. Dumbbell RDL or barbell RDL from rack (moderate load) — 3 x 6–8
5. Single-leg glute bridge with pause — 3 x 8–10
6. Suitcase carry or loaded carry for 40–60 s — 3 sets

Day C — Upper 2
1. Warm-up
2. Seated dumbbell/neutral-grip shoulder press — 4 x 6–8
3. Neutral-grip pull-ups or assisted pull-ups / heavy lat pulldown — 4 x 6–8
4. Chest-supported single-arm row or one-arm cable — 3 x 8–10
5. Lateral raises — 3 x 12–15
6. Anti-extension rollouts (wheel) or plank with progressions — 3 x 8–12 or 3 x 45–60 s planks

Day D — Lower 2
1. Warm-up
2. Front-loaded goblet/zercher squat alternative — Goblet or Zercher (if cleared) 4 x 6–8 OR pause box squats using dumbbells — 4 x 6–8
   - Zercher requires care; if uncomfortable, stick to goblet or machine leg press with controlled depth.
3. Bulgarian split squat (heavier) — 3 x 6–8 each
4. Romanian deadlift (heavier, controlled) — 3 x 6–8
5. Hamstring machine or Nordic curl progression — 3 x 6–10
6. Anti-rotation core: cable or band chops — 3 x 10 each side

Progression notes for Phase 2
- Push intensity up modestly but avoid maximal loads that produce spinal compression or pain. If pain arises, scale back.
- Longer carries build core and trunk tolerance; use heavier carries as tolerated.

Phase 3 — Strength consolidation & power/conditioning (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: consolidate strength gains, add short power/tempo elements (safe lower-back loading), refine conditioning and resiliency, maintain spine-sparing constraints.

Weekly layout remains 4 gym days, but add brief power/tempo movements and slightly lower rep ranges for main lifts.

Weeks 9–12: session details (changes/highlights)

Day A — Upper 1 (Strength + speed)
1. Warm-up
2. Dumbbell bench press (heavier) — 4 x 5–6
3. Bent-over row alternative: chest-supported row heavy — 4 x 5–6 (avoid loaded spinal flexion)
4. Incline push + row superset (machine) — 3 x 6–8
5. Plyometric push-up progression (bodyweight) or med-ball chest pass — 3 x 6–8 (only if comfortable)
6. Face pulls / band pull-aparts — 3 x 12
7. Farmer carry heavy — 3 x 60 s

Day B — Lower 1 (Strength & power from hips)
1. Warm-up
2. Trap-bar deadlift (heavier but controlled) — 4 x 4–5 (keep RPE 7–8 and perfect hinge)
3. Box step-ups or loaded split squat — 3 x 6–8 each
4. Barbell RDL from pins / dumbbell RDL — 3 x 6
5. Kettlebell swing (light–moderate, hip-hinge explosive) — 3 x 10–15 (monitor lumbar comfort)
6. Core: weighted plank or RKC plank progressions — 3 x 30–45 s

Day C — Upper 2 (Strength)
1. Warm-up
2. Seated military press (dumbbell) — 4 x 5–6
3. Pull-up or heavy lat pulldown — 4 x 5–6
4. Single-arm dumbbell row heavy — 3 x 6–8
5. Lateral raise dropsets — 3 x 10–15
6. Anti-rotation and anti-extension core work — 3 x 10–12

Day D — Lower 2 (Hypertrophy & unilateral)
1. Warm-up
2. Goblet or Zercher squat (moderate-heavy) — 4 x 6–8 (keep depth comfortable)
3. Reverse lunges / walking lunges — 3 x 8 each
4. Single-leg RDL heavy — 3 x 6–8
5. Hamstring curl / glute-ham raise — 3 x 8–10
6. Carries / core finishers — 3 x 45–60 s

Deload week option
- If client has poor recovery or fatigue in week 8 or 12, replace session volumes with 50–60% volume for one week or take an active recovery week (lighter weights, fewer sets).

Exercise selection notes & spine-safety specifics
- Avoid heavy axial loaded flexion: No heavy bent-over barbell rows with back rounding, no heavy barbell back squats to maximal loads, no heavy loaded forward flexion under load. If a row is needed, prefer chest-supported row, single-arm row, or cable rows which let torso stay supported.
- Use trap-bar deadlifts instead of conventional deadlifts when possible because they reduce shear on lumbar and allow more upright torso. RDLs are allowed if technique is excellent and loads moderate—emphasize hip hinge and neutral spine.
- Goblet/zercher/front-loaded variants are preferred over heavy back squats because they encourage upright torso and less symmetrical compressive shear but still monitor depth and tolerance. Leg press and hack squat machines can be used to increase leg strength without high spinal load.
- Core work focuses on anti-extension (planks, RKC), anti-rotation (Pallof press, suitcase carry), and dynamic stability (deadbug, bird-dog). Avoid loaded spinal flexion (sit-ups with heavy load, heavy loaded crunches) that flex the lumbar spine under load repetitively.

Mobility, recovery and daily practices
- Daily: 5–10 min thoracic mobility (foam roller T-spine extensions), hip flexor stretches, hamstring mobility, glute activation (clams, band lateral walks).
- Workday breaks: every 30–45 minutes stand, diaphragmatic breathing for 1–2 min, gentle extension posture work to counter prolonged flexion.
- Sleep: aim for 7–9 hours per night.
- Recovery tools: regular physiotherapy check-ins as needed, soft tissue work (foam roll/glute release), avoid prolonged sitting without breaks.
- Pain management: If any radicular pain, numbness, or new neurological symptoms appear, stop lifting and refer to physio/doctor.

Nutrition (high-level)
- Goal: support strength gains and recovery. Target zone (example) depending on goals:
  - Maintenance/lean gain: 10–12 kcal per lb bodyweight (adjust to client’s goals). If weight loss desired, 300–500 kcal deficit; for muscle gain, 200–300 kcal surplus.
  - Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight per day (roughly 0.7–1.0 g/lb).
  - Carbs: prioritize around workouts (pre/post) to fuel performance and recovery.
  - Fats: ~20–30% of total calories.
- Hydration: at least 2–3 L/day, more with sweat.
- Timing: aim for a protein-containing meal within 1–2 hours post-workout.

Monitoring & progression cues
- Track RPE, sets, and reps each session. Increase weight by ~2.5–5% when prescribed reps can be done with good form for two consecutive sessions.
- Prioritize technique over load—stop any set if lumbar extension, rounding, or pain occurs.
- Use session notes to flag any symptoms to share with physio if needed.

Sample microprogression (example for trap-bar DL)
- Week 1–2: 3 x 6 at RPE 6 (learn pattern)
- Week 3–4: 3 x 6 at RPE 7 (increase weight 5–10%)
- Week 5–6: 4 x 5 at RPE 7–8
- Week 7–8: 4 x 5 at RPE 7–8 (increase weight as tolerated)
- Week 9–10: 4 x 4 at RPE 8
- Week 11–12: 4 x 4 at RPE 8 (peak intensity while monitoring)

Final points for you as the trainer
- Keep communication open with the client’s physio. Ask for any specific restrictions beyond “no heavy spinal loading and no loaded spinal flexion”.
- Start conservatively; the client’s history warrants caution. Progress to heavier loads if tolerance is excellent.
- Emphasize posture, breathing, and gradual overload. Use machine and unilateral alternatives liberally.
- If you’d like, I can convert this plan to a printable week-by-week spreadsheet, or produce session-by-session templates (weights to track) if you give the client’s current PRs/starting weights and goals (fat loss, muscle gain, performance).

Would you like the program formatted into a week-by-week printable table or a 12-week calendar you can hand the client? Any specific goals (body composition, performance targets) or any other contra-indications from the physio?
